This tutorial applies full-text retrieval to corpora in several languages. The [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) tutorial uses one novel in English; this one indexes three corpora:

| Corpus Identifier | Source Collection | Language | Volume | Retrieval Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `gutenberg-en` | Project Gutenberg | English | 100 volumes | Paragraph |
| `gutenberg-es` | Project Gutenberg | Spanish | 100 volumes | Paragraph |
| `wikipedia-en` | Wikipedia (2023-11-01 dump) | English | 1,000 articles | Paragraph |

### Motivation for Paragraph-Level Granularity

Indexing a long document, such as a complete book or an encyclopedia article, as a single unit reduces precision. A long document covers several topics, and the document frequency of a term carries little information when most terms of the vocabulary occur in almost every document. A **paragraph** is a shorter unit, restricted to one topic, and is therefore appropriate both for matching a query and for fitting a text model.

---

## Dataset Preparation

The datasets and the text profiles used in this tutorial are produced by `tutorials/prepare.jl`. The script downloads texts in the public domain, divides them into paragraphs, fits the text profiles, and indexes the corpora:

```sh
# Complete build (approximately one hour)
julia -t 8 --project=tutorials tutorials/prepare.jl

# Reduced build, for verification (approximately five minutes)
julia -t 8 --project=tutorials tutorials/prepare.jl --smoke
```

Each stage (`corpora`, `profiles`, `projects`) writes its result to disk, so a later execution repeats only the stages that are missing. A single stage can also be requested by name, and `--force` rebuilds it: `julia -t 8 --project=tutorials tutorials/prepare.jl projects --force`.

The times reported in this page were measured with 8 threads. Indexing uses them, so a different number of threads changes the values in the last table.

::: {.callout-note}
## Quarto Rendering Configuration

When rendering this manual via Quarto on systems where `/run/user/$UID` is restricted, configure a custom runtime directory:

```sh
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$(mktemp -d) quarto render manual
```
:::

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(pwd(), "..", "..", "tutorials"); io=devnull)

import SimilaritySearchEngine as SSE
import TextSearch
import SimilaritySearch
using JSON3
using Printf

const TUT = normpath(joinpath(pwd(), "..", "..", "tutorials"))
const DATA = joinpath(TUT, "data")
const PROFILES = joinpath(TUT, "profiles")
const PROJECTS = joinpath(TUT, "projects")

const SUFFIX = isfile(joinpath(DATA, "manifest.json")) ? "" :
               isfile(joinpath(DATA, "manifest-smoke.json")) ? "-smoke" :
               error("""
    This page requires datasets built by tutorials/prepare.jl.
    Execute from the repository root:
        julia --project=tutorials tutorials/prepare.jl
    (or use `--smoke` for a lightweight build)""")

const MANIFEST = JSON3.read(read(joinpath(DATA, "manifest$SUFFIX.json"), String))
const NAMES = ["gutenberg-en", "gutenberg-es", "wikipedia-en"]

corpus_file(name) = joinpath(DATA, name * SUFFIX * ".jsonl")
profile_file(name) = joinpath(PROFILES, name * SUFFIX * ".zip")
project_root() = SUFFIX == "" ? PROJECTS : joinpath(PROJECTS, "smoke")

function first_record(name)
    open(corpus_file(name)) do io
        JSON3.read(readline(io))
    end
end

thousands(n) = replace(string(n), r"(?<=\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => ",")

quiet(f) = redirect_stderr(devnull) do
    f()
end
nothing
```

## Corpus Statistics

```{julia}
#| echo: false
SUFFIX == "" ||
    println("NOTE: Evaluated against a smoke build. Values reflect the reduced smoke dataset.")
```

The preparation script generates one JSONL file per corpus, recording structural measurements dynamically:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
using Markdown
rows = ["| Corpus | Language | Documents | Paragraphs | Paragraphs / Document | Storage Size |",
        "| :--- | :--- | ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:|"]
for n in NAMES
    c = MANIFEST.corpora[Symbol(n)]
    push!(rows, @sprintf("| `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %.1f | %.1f MB |",
                         n, c.lang, thousands(c.documents), thousands(c.paragraphs),
                         c.paragraphs / max(c.documents, 1), c.megabytes))
end
Markdown.parse(join(rows, "\n"))
```

### Statistical Observations

1. **Variation in the length of encyclopedia articles**: a long Wikipedia article contains many more paragraphs than a short entry.
2. **Variation in the length of books**: in the Project Gutenberg collections, the size of a volume ranges from a short pamphlet to a work in several volumes. Indexing by paragraph gives units of comparable size for documents of any length.

Each JSONL record contains the text of one paragraph and the metadata of its source:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
r = first_record("gutenberg-es")
println("Metadata Keys: ", join(String.(keys(r)), ", "))
println()
println("Document ID:   ", r.doc_id)
println("Title / Author: ", r.title, " — ", r.author)
println("Text Preview:  ", first(r.text, 240), "…")
```

---

## Linguistic Profiles (`TextProfile`)

A text project requires a [`TextProfile`](https://sadit.github.io/TextSearch.jl/dev/api/), which defines the tokenization of the vocabulary, the term weighting, the stopword list, the lemma map, and the query-expansion network.

The preparation script fits the profiles with the procedure of `TextSearch.jl` (`textsearch fit`). That procedure applies Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) to obtain word embeddings, and builds the query-expansion structures from them.

### Normalization Policy: Preserving Case and Diacritics

The corpora are processed under the following normalization configuration:

```toml
[normalization]
del_diac = false      # Preserve diacritical marks (e.g., accents)
lc = false            # Preserve character casing
del_punc = true       # Remove punctuation marks
group_num = true      # Normalize numeric sequences
group_url = true      # Normalize URL strings
```

Preserving case and diacritics preserves distinctions in meaning, for example between a proper noun and a common noun, or between two words of a Romance language that differ only in an accent. The query is resolved against this vocabulary, and a query written without accents is mapped to the accented form at search time.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
profiles = Dict(n => TextSearch.load_profile(profile_file(n)) for n in NAMES)
rows = ["| Profile | Vocabulary Size | Stopwords | Lemmas | Expansion Entries | Fit Time |",
        "| :--- | ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:|"]
for n in NAMES
    p = profiles[n]
    m = MANIFEST.profiles[Symbol(n)]
    mark(applied) = applied ? " *(applied)*" : ""
    push!(rows, @sprintf("| `%s` | %s | %s%s | %s%s | %s%s | %.0fs |",
                         n, thousands(TextSearch.vocsize(p.model.voc)),
                         thousands(length(p.stopwords)), mark(p.applied.stopwords),
                         thousands(length(p.lemmas)), mark(p.applied.lemmas),
                         thousands(length(p.query_expansion)), mark(p.applied.query_expansion),
                         m.fit_seconds))
end
Markdown.parse(join(rows, "\n"))
```

### Applied vs. Carried Artifacts

A fitted profile stores its lemma clusters and its expansion network, and does not apply them by default. Applying one of them modifies the tokenization, and the project configuration selects it explicitly. The stopwords are marked as applied because the vocabulary frequencies were computed with the stopwords removed.

The profile records its origin and the parameters used to fit it:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
show(profiles["wikipedia-en"])
```

---

## Query Execution and Ranking

Search queries evaluate against the indexed BM25 inverted files:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
handles = Dict{String,Any}()
quiet() do
    for n in NAMES
        handles[n] = SSE.open_project(project_root(), n; read_only=true)
    end
end

function show_hits(name, query; k=3, policy=SSE.QueryPolicy())
    h = handles[name]
    println("[", name, "] Query: ", query)
    for (i, r) in enumerate(quiet(() -> SSE.ftsearch(h, query, k; policy)))
        items = SSE.fetch_items(h, [r._id])
        isempty(items) && continue
        it = only(items)
        src = get(it.meta, "title", "?")
        para = replace(something(it.payload, ""), r"\s+" => " ")
        @printf("  %d. %-42s | Distance: %.3f\n", i, first(src, 42), r.distance)
        println("     ", first(para, 150), length(para) > 150 ? "…" : "")
    end
    println()
end
nothing
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
show_hits("gutenberg-en", "the whale rose out of the sea")
show_hits("gutenberg-es", "Fortunata y Jacinta en Madrid")
show_hits("wikipedia-en", "anarchism as a political philosophy")
```

The reported distances are BM25 scores with the sign inverted, which follows the convention of `SimilaritySearch.jl`: a smaller value indicates a closer match.

---

## Orthographic Query Correction

Because linguistic profiles preserve diacritics, unaccented search terms (e.g., `musica`) do not match accented vocabulary entries (`música`) by default. 

Under the default `QueryPolicy(correction=:auto)`, the query resolution engine identifies unaccented query terms and maps them to their most probable accented vocabulary counterparts:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
for q in ["la musica del corazon", "el pais y la republica"]
    println("Query: ", q)
    for line in SSE.ftexplain(handles["gutenberg-es"], q)
        println("  ~ ", line)
    end
    println()
end
```

`ftexplain` reports the token substitutions that were applied. A query written with correct orthography produces no substitution:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
println("ftexplain output on correctly typed query: ",
        SSE.ftexplain(handles["gutenberg-es"], "la música del corazón"))
```

To enforce exact literal matching without orthographic correction, set `correction=:off`:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
show_hits("gutenberg-es", "la musica del corazon"; k=2)
show_hits("gutenberg-es", "la musica del corazon"; k=2, policy=SSE.QueryPolicy(correction=:off))
```

---

## Semantic Query Expansion

Query expansion adds to each query term its nearest neighbors in the LSI embedding space:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
p = profiles["wikipedia-en"]
for tok in ["anarchism", "philosophy", "revolution"]
    ns = get(p.query_expansion, tok, nothing)
    println(@sprintf("%-14s -> %s", tok, ns === nothing ? "(not present in expansion network)" : join(first(ns, 6), ", ")))
end
```

Query expansion increases recall, because it adds related terms to the query:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
show_hits("wikipedia-en", "anarchism"; k=2)
show_hits("wikipedia-en", "anarchism"; k=2, policy=SSE.QueryPolicy(expansion=false))
```

---

## Programmatic Project Lifecycle

The following example performs the complete sequence over a subset of one corpus:

```julia
# 1. Ingest slice of paragraph records
slice = map(Iterators.take(eachline(corpus_file("gutenberg-en")), 2000)) do line
    o = JSON3.read(line)
    meta = Dict{String,Any}(String(k) => v for (k, v) in pairs(o) if k !== :text && k !== :doc_id)
    SSE.TextItem(String(o.text); doc_id=String(o.doc_id), meta)
end

# 2. Create project using a pre-computed BaseProfile
workdir = mktempdir()
h = SSE.create_project(workdir, "sample_project";
        engine    = SSE.FullTextEngine,
        backend   = TextSearch.BM25InvertedFile,
        textmodel = SSE.BaseProfile(profiles["gutenberg-en"]))

# 3. Stage items (durable on disk, pending indexing)
SSE.append_items!(h, slice)

# 4. Construct inverted file postings over staged backlog
quiet() do
    SSE.index!(h)
end

# 5. Execute full-text query
results = SSE.ftsearch(h, "the whale", 3)
```

---

## Empirical Benchmark Analysis

The following table reports the construction and indexing times measured over the three corpora:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
rows = ["| Project | Paragraphs | Vocabulary | Create (s) | Append (s) | Index (s) | Indexing Latency (ms/doc) | Disk Footprint |",
        "| :--- | ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:| ---:|"]
for n in NAMES
    p = MANIFEST.projects[Symbol(n)]
    push!(rows, @sprintf("| `%s` | %s | %s | %.0fs | %.0fs | %.0fs | %.2f | %.0f MB |",
                         n, thousands(p.paragraphs), thousands(p.vocsize),
                         p.create_seconds, p.append_seconds, p.index_seconds,
                         p.index_ms_per_paragraph, p.megabytes))
end
Markdown.parse(join(rows, "\n"))
```

### Performance Observations

- **Cost of persistence**: writing each document to RocksDB adds little time compared with an indexing loop in memory, and the data survive an interruption of the process.
- **Compilation time**: the first execution in Julia includes the compilation of the code. Later batches show the rate of the compiled code.
- **Storage of the profile**: creating a project with a fitted profile writes that profile into the RocksDB store of the project, so the project can be copied to another machine without additional files.
- **Storage of the index**: a text project stores the inverted index, so opening it does not index the corpus again. The [architecture guide](../architecture.qmd) reports the difference: 1.4 s against 20.4 s for the largest of these corpora.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
for h in values(handles)
    SSE.close_project!(h)
end
```
